result: Backend tests and frontend build pass. Source-RCON framing, loopback connection, serialized requests, 2-second timeout, input bounds, running/unavailable guards, live-control rate limiting, CSRF/audit group integration, per-process credential generation, stop/exit cleanup, and UI polling cleanup are present. Material gaps remain: SourceRconClient does not validate authentication response or packet request IDs/types, and mutation endpoints discard the RCON response and always return 204 after transport success, so an RCON auth/command error response could be falsely reported as successful. The Players UI exposes persistent-list add/delete controls to viewers even though backend authorization rejects them. Start failure can leave RconEndpoint populated until a later lifecycle path. No fallback command path is implemented, so there is no fallback success claim, but this differs from the architected degraded fallback expectation.

evidence.outcome: Passed; Vite production build completed with existing SignalR Rollup annotation warnings.

RCON uses loopback, semaphore, linked 2-second timeout, Source-RCON packet framing, and bounded response size; auth response status/id/type are not checked and ExecuteAsync does not interpret command errors.
Live mutations return NoContent whenever LivePlayerService completes without throwing; RCON error payloads can be presented as success.
Per-process random RCON endpoint is loopback-only, not Docker-published, and cleared on normal stop/exit; start exception can leave stale endpoint state.
Live polling runs every 10 seconds and clears its interval; kick/ban/chat confirmations and role-gated controls exist, but persistent player-list add/delete controls are shown to viewers.

next_slice.summary: Fix RCON auth/response validation and propagate command failures before returning success; clear RconEndpoint on failed startup; hide persistent-list mutations for viewers or provide explicit forbidden UI. Add packet/auth/command-error fixture tests and endpoint integration coverage.

blockers: RCON auth and command response statuses are not validated, allowing false success for failed live mutations.
Viewer UI exposes persistent-list mutation controls despite backend denial.
